answer: Before grading, the verifier pins a 64 GB delta array in RAM and fires latency probes at pseudo-random offsets with a 500-nanosecond budget per probe. A late or wrong probe ends the round at once. One honest agent rents a single 64 GB slice for about $12 a month and serves one probe stream; ten fakes must rent 640 GB and serve ten streams in parallel, ten times the memory and power. A failed probe fails verification, the bond is slashed, and the vault identity stays frozen until a spiral recheck clears it.
